The Chariot Bug is a low-ranking species functioning as scouts and load bearers in Arachnid colonies. They don't form much of a threat when forced into combat roles because of their light armor, slow speed and weak bite.
Drone Bugs are an Arachnid caste that look like juvenile versions of the Warrior type. Their exoskeletons are less hardened, making them more vulnerable but also lighter and faster.
The Warrior Bug is a basic but effective melee fighter, available in virtually limitless numbers to the Arachnids. They lead the charge to overwhelm and overrun the enemy.
The Tiger Bug is a stronger sub-species of the Warrior type. Their tough exoskeletons are more resistant to light weapons and require armor-piercing capabilities to counter effectively.

A heavily evolved variant of the Warrior bug, the Royal Guard obtained its name from being frequently encountered while protecting colonies that included a Brain or Queen bug.\n\nThese Arachnids are exceptionally tough and are known to become even more ferocious once they have received critical injuries.

• Will "enrage" when its hit points are fully depleted\n• When enraged, its hit points are reset once while movement speed is permanently reduced\n• Dies when the rage timer expires or if its replenished hit points are depleted,

The Spitter Bug is a fragile species that can project acid from a thoracic gland. This substance causes serious corrosion and can even be lethal when exposed to substantial doses.\n\nThey are known to operate effectively in concert with Warrior bugs: One providing suppressive fire, while the other forms a meat-shield and closes in for the kill.

With each Arachnid having evolved to serve a well-defined role, the Tanker Bug functions as a form of assault tank. It has thick armor and the ability to spray a stream of flammable, corrosive liquid.

Hoppers are flying Arachnids that serve as air support and excel at suppressing enemies with constant harassment. These creatures are swift and agile, but their lightly armored bodies make them vulnerable to concentrated fire.

There is a radio tower ahead of your position.
Get up that slope and bring that station online.
The battle of Klendathu. A day that will live in infamy.
But from tragedy springs hope, as the Federation rebuilds its fleet bigger and stronger than before.
To fuel this war machine, all eyes are now on Kwalasha.
Once an isolated outpost, this mineral-rich world has become a key part of humanity's battle for survival.
But the planet's vital mining industry may now be in danger after reports of Bugs on the surface.
And so the Mobile Infantry answer humanity’s call! These brave men and women will defend Kwalasha from any insect aggression.
With the size of the Bug problem now clear, immediate action is needed.
The Mobile Infantry moves into gear to protect Kwalasha, its mines, and its people.
Kwalashans take great pride in their planet’s mining industry. Through sweat of brow, valiant colonists dig up the precious minerals the Federation needs.
It’s an ore effort for the war effort!
And they’re not going to let a few Bugs scare them off!
The Mobile Infantry has begun escorting workers, many of them patriotic volunteers, back into the mines so they can keep excavating the future of humanity!
Federation scientists ask - Who turned off the lights?
Rolling blackouts plague the planet as bugs target Kwalasha’s electrical grid. Industry grinds to a halt, threatening to paralyze the war effort.
Military operations are underway to retake the critical power station and nip these outages in the bud.
The Mobile Infantry will get the job done!
There’s danger afoot, underfoot! The Bugs lurk in subterranean tunnels, preparing for their next vicious attack.
Wiping out these nests is dangerous work, but nothing the Mobile Infantry can’t handle.
Our brave troopers will uncover and eradicate the enemy wherever they hide!
The only thing worse than a Bug… is a traitor!
After a string of civilian deaths, subversive elements are using the mining tragedy to push their own false agenda.
One such rabble rouser is Thomas Rees, leader of the Kwalashan Miners’ Union. In times of war, dissent is deadly and will not be tolerated.
Execution tonight at 6, all net, all channels.
Attacks are reported across Kwalasha, overwhelming local defenses.
But hope is not lost. The tide of insects will meet their match at Fort Meru, the Mobile Infantry’s formidable base of operations.
From their new headquarters in high orbit to oversee the conflict, Military Command has expressed their full confidence in Meru’s ability to withstand the coming siege.
Peace and prosperity! After the bugs’ defeat, Kwalasha has become an oasis of calm in a violent galaxy.
Grateful colonists enjoy an idyllic life working in the mines, safe under the Federation’s watchful eye.
The Mobile Infantry stands vigilant, ready to respond to any threat, big or small. Even in peacetime, there’s still work to do.
Just today, a group of miners were trapped underground after a cave-in.
Hang tight down there, boys! Help is on the way!
Fort Meru has fallen to the Bugs… Now it’s humanity’s turn to strike back!
Federation forces launch a massive counterattack to cleanse the planet.
In the air and on the ground, they’ll deliver a swift one-two punch that’ll catch the Bugs off guard.
Their superior numbers are no match for the Federation’s superior tactics.
A bitter setback for humanity! Thousands are dead after the military’s failed offensive.
In this dark hour, the fate of Kwalasha hangs by a thread. But one thing that remains undefeated is the courage of the brave men and women of the Mobile Infantry.
Groups of survivors are scattered across the planet’s harsh desert, struggling to return to civilization and jump back into the fight.
They haven’t given up, and neither shall we!
No more intelligence leaks! Psychic Operatives have discovered the Bugs’ despicable methods for stealing our secrets.
And just in time: Federation scientists are developing a new wonder weapon to annihilate the Arachnid threat.
And it is Kwalashan industry that is providing the key material components behind this miracle of military engineering.
Citizens can rest easy knowing its secrets are safe from prying Bug eyes.
All out war rages on Kwalasha.
Federatsiyagrad, the planet’s capital, is the scene of bitter fighting as the Mobile Infantry mount a stalwart defense against the invading bug hordes.
Local forces are surrounded - but help is on the way.
The Sky Marshal vows “Not one step back!”, dispatching the full might of human technology to hold the line.
Bugs infest the intricate mazes of pipes and tunnels beneath Federatsiyagrad, using these subterranean passages to roam freely throughout the city.
Mobile Infantry forces storm underground to kick out the Arachnid intruders. They don’t mind a little dirt and grime, not when there’s bugs to kill!
For weeks, Kwalasha’s capital has been an urban battlefield.
The fight for Federatsiyagrad is now a war of attrition, as brave defenders hold back what seems like an endless tide of Arachnid warriors.
But after this long ordeal, victory is finally within reach.
A powerful counterattack is being planned to drive out the Bugs and save the city.
And stay out! Arachnid forces are on the run after the Mobile Infantry routs them from the city.
To prevent further incursions, the military is building a line of fortification around Kwalasha’s industrial sector.
Troopers are busy clearing out the last few insect stragglers from the green zone.
Safety, security, and a return to normal life are just around the bend!
A heavy price has been paid for Kwalasha’s freedom - but victory is closer than ever!
Fleeing our superior airpower, the Bugs have retreated into deep underground caves that even our bombs can’t reach.
While the Fleet keeps them pinned down, the M.I. mobilizes for a final assault on Arachnid territory.
BREAKING NEWS: The Fleet’s main airbase is under attack! Bugs have breached the safety zone, finding a weak spot in the surrounding ring of steel.
This targeted assault seems designed to cripple our aerial capabilities. Losing those strike craft would be a fatal setback for the coming offensive!
The Sky Marshal’s master plan revealed: lure the enemy out of hiding with the temptation of an easy victory! And after letting them in, we’ve slammed the door behind them.
M.I forces have recaptured a key defence post, blocking off the mountain pass and sealing the Bugs in open desert.
Caught by the jaws of a steel trap, those vermin have nowhere to run, nowhere to hide. Easy pickings for our airstrikes!
Let’s finish the job! With Arachnid corpses littering the burning sands, it’s finally time to stamp out the Bug infestation on Kwalasha.
Federation troops surround the last remnant of hostile territory and begin their march towards victory.
To end the war over the planet, only one question remains: Where is the Brain Bug?
One gifted psychic officer has unraveled the Bugs’ secret strategy to conquer Kwalasha.
But his shuttle has gone down deep in Bug territory and now a desperate rescue is mounted to recover him and the vital knowledge he possesses.
The Mobile Infantry never leave a comrade behind.
The Bug menace on Kwalasha has been exterminated.
The Federation’s victory is a victory for all humankind, bringing prosperity and harmony to this troubled world.
It’s a system that protects, a system that works, a system that needs planets like Kwalasha to keep the fight going on all fronts.

Planet Varuna, home to Mahanagar, a giant in the economic market and one of the most brightly shining cities in the Federation.
Built on the Ganda River, the island city offers natural protection against the Arachnid presence on the planet.
While the odd stray Arachnid may slip through the net,
the real fight is against the criminals who seek to disturb the peaceful lives of our citizens.
But justice is carried out by the likes of Officer Kayla Keys.
The local police negotiator is en route to the crime scene.
We now take you live to Mahanagar to follow the progress of this story.
An outbreak of Arachnids in the northern district of Mahanagar has prompted the Mobile Infantry to mount an armed response.
On occasion, small pockets of Bugs will manage to tunnel their way below the shallow marshlands.
For the safety of citizens, a Mobile Infantry detachment remains permanently stationed in the city.
These brave troopers have arrived at the local railway station to clear the streets by sunrise.
Their service guarantees your safe morning commute!
Further Bug-related incidents have been reported across the outer districts of Mahanagar.
Governor Govac has issued his assurance that the situation is under control,
and that citizens in the city center will remain safe to go on with their day unperturbed.
Drums of gunfire may be heard occasionally across the hot zones.
That’s the comforting sound of our troopers driving the Bugs back into the river!
The Arachnid outbreak in Mahanagar has grown in scale.
Accepting responsibility for the debacle, Governor Govac has resigned from his position,
placing the city under martial law as his last official act.
The Bugs must be stopped in their march toward the central district, and Terran Command has the answer:
The tactical destruction of all district bridges!
TAC fighters operating from the city starport are already in flight to execute this plan with pinpoint destructive precision!
The Arachnid march has been thwarted after the victorious destruction of Mahanagar's main bridges.
But reports have shown the Bugs are now digging into the metro system to continue their advance through the underground.
Is there a Brain Bug on planet Varuna?
Federal scientists are investigating the well orchestrated movements of the Arachnids.
To defeat the Bug, we must stay one step ahead!
The enemy may think they control the board, but our new gambit will put them in check!
The presence of a Brain Bug leading the attacks on Mahanagar has been confirmed.
Now that we know our enemy, we have the means to defeat it!
Federal scientists have exposed a major weakness in the Arachnid's offensive capabilities.
Armed with this tactical knowledge, the advanced water systems of Mahanagar will be used to flood the outer districts.
Tens of thousands of Bugs will drown, and the Brain Bug will remain trapped and isolated in the city center.
Flooding the outer districts of Mahanagar has dealt the Arachnid invasion a heavy blow!

The starport of Mahanagar has fallen.
The Brain Bug has directed its remaining hordes to disrupt the shipments of new equipment and personnel at this vital transport hub.

Total victory is close at hand in Mahanagar!
No escape, tricks, or countermoves remain for the Bug!

Many did their part and gave their life in service of a great cause: protecting the wellbeing of our citizens.
The city, too, has paid a heavy toll...

Listen up, troopers! A major update has been released, adding a ton of improvements and (free) new content! Many of the campaign and challenge missions have been updated and now include new player units. In particular the Kwalasha and Gehenna campaigns have seen significant changes and now use the Materiel resource as a requisite to deploying turrets and advanced units. In addition to all of the above, this update includes significant performance improvements, specifically targeting the slowdowns you may experience during long play sessions and on larger maps. Note that due to all these changes savegames from previous versions are no longer compatible. If you try to load an older savegame you will get a prompt to restart the scenario instead. Below is a selection of missions that highlight these new units as well as some of the units that have received significant design changes.

original: Territory Mode offers a new way to play, with a focus on freedom of choice and tactics. It features new maps crafted specifically for the game mode. You'll battle the Arachnids for control of Territory Points, which provide a steady flow of resources - adding a fresh strategic layer to the game.

Each territory point you control will give you Resources over time. It is vital to secure each of these points to ensure your Resource income can support the cost of war.

Resources are needed for:
• Unlocking new Technologies
• Calling Reinforcements for weakened units
• Calling in new units
• Paying the upkeep cost of your units and turrets
• Constructing and upgrading Turrets
• Filling Supply Depots to increase your Supply

Useful tips:
• When you disband a unit, its Resource cost is refunded.
• Reinforcements for weakened units are 50% cheaper than purchasing a new unit

Supplies are required to deploy units on the battlefield. To support a larger army, you need more supplies.
In Territory Mode, you can gain more supplies by deploying Supply depots on the Delivery Platforms that are attached to your main base and other Radio Stations on the map.

To deploy a Supply Depot:
• Select the empty Delivery Platform
• Click the 'Request Supplies' button
• Wait for the upgrade to complete

Note that you must have enough resources stockpiled to pay for the cost of the Upgrade. Each time you upgrade another Delivery Platform, the cost for the next Upgrade will increase.

Materiel is required to deploy Turrets and specific types of advanced units on the battlefield. 
In Territory Mode, you can gain more Materiel by deploying Materiel Depots on the delivery platforms that are attached to your Main Base and other Radio Stations on the map.

To deploy a Materiel Depot:
• Select an empty Delivery Platform
• Click the 'Materiel Depot' button
• Wait for the upgrade to complete

Note that you must have enough Resources stockpiled to pay for the cost of the Upgrade. Each time you upgrade another Delivery Platform, the cost for the next Upgrade will increase.

Researching Technologies is an essential part of the Territory Mode. Each Battle Group has a different set of technologies available to them. These are used for:

• Unlocking new Unit Types

You can access the Technology panel by clicking on the 'Technologies' button at the bottom of the screen.

Welcome to Ghutana, Commander. I've been looking forward to your arrival...

The planet - and its Arachnid colonies - are ideally suited for our experimental weapons programs--chemical, nuclear, you name it. It's remote, it's quiet, and it's the perfect place to see what our new toys can really do.
I'm patching you through to Doctor Kraus now. He's the lead for our R&D department on-site. Try to stay on his good side...
Commander. Our research here is vital for the security of the Federation. The Arachnids possess a level of... biological efficiency that we must fully understand to ensure our dominance.
We have a test missile launch scheduled for today, but an Arachnid host attacked and overran the facility. I need you to regain control.
I'll be monitoring your vitals and combat tactics throughout the mission. It should make for an interesting study.
Start by securing the launch control center; it will serve as your foothold for the operation.
Ah, our Eradicator squads. Their ammunition utilizes localized radiation to induce rapid internal necrosis in the target; it is quite a thorough process.
As for your Arachnid escort, do not let their presence unsettle you. Through pheromonal recalibration, we have co-opted their predatory instincts to serve our interests.
Unlike your soldiers, they are free from any psychological limitations - they simply exist to kill. A fascinating display of biological utility.
Commander... If you're going to make extensive use of our Arachnid control program, make sure you deploy enough pheromone silos.
You are approaching the launch platform. A powerful weapon, certainly, though quite crude in its delivery.
Well done. The launch site is secured--ensure it stays that way.
However, we still require access to the hangar for refueling operations. It appears the Arachnids have already established a nest within the structure-- a fascinating use of our infrastructure.
You'll have to clear them out, Commander.
The fuel cells are now in transit. Ensure they reach the launch platform unimpeded.
Incoming signatures are spiking. It's fascinating... they seem to possess an instinctual awareness of the threat we've prepared for them.
Refueling cycle complete. Clear the platform, Commander; the launch window is narrow, and I have no intention of further delaying the sequence.
Great work down there, Commander. I'll have your mission debriefing ready by the time you reach orbit. Drinks are on me. Out.
Do not lose the main base
Do not lose the Eradicator squads
Clear the sector and capture the Hydra
Commander, we know why the Hydra did not show up. Tracing the swarm of Acid Grenadiers back to its source led us to a massive lair... filled with millions of eggs.
Right at the center of it all: our Hydra. The creature is a hive queen, Commander, with maternal instincts far outweighing the lure of my Pheromone Emitter!
Now we must proceed with care. This is a priceless opportunity to study the Arachnid reproductive systems.
Clear out the surrounding nests and secure a perimeter around the lair. Do not touch the Hydra until further instructions.
That's one hive cleared. Good work!
Another hive cleared - just one more to go.
Very well. The perimeter has been established.
Commander, secure a cluster of Hydra eggs and send it to my lab. And restrain yourself - I need them intact.
I have received the eggs--and they appear unscathed. Exterminate the remaining clusters at your leisure.
Commander, secure the northern station for the deployment of the D.I.M. Dart Launcher. This location provides a clear line of fire into the Hydra's lair.
Initiating deployment of the D.I.M. Dart Launcher now.
Great work, Commander. Hold this position until Kraus is ready to activate the launcher.
Do not provoke the Hydra yet. I'm aware this procedure requires a level of nuance and intellect your branch is not well known for. Complete your tasks and follow my instructions to the letter.
All preparations are completed! Engage the Hydra, Commander. We need its armor weakened enough to allow the D.I.M. Dart to penetrate into the nerve stem.
As for the surrounding swarm, exterminate them all. They are of no scientific value.
The Hydra has been sufficiently weakened! Target coordinates synchronized with the D.I.M. Dart Launcher.
Magnificent. The Hydra is responsive! All my work has finally come to fruition.
Doctor... I've got massive Bug activity lighting up in all surrounding sectors. They're converging on your position, Commander...
Commander! Protect the Hydra with everything you have! I'll see you all dead before I lose this specimen!
Wait... I'll direct it... I'll turn it against the incoming swarms! Form a perimeter around the Hydra, and I'll demonstrate what this magnificent beast can truly do!
The neural-link is holding perfectly. My work here is a triumph. The Hercules Program is a resounding success.
The data is conclusive--the neural-link is holding perfectly! I'm transferring the Hydra to the Research Division's high-security transport immediately.
You have served your purpose here, Commander. A positive evaluation all in all. You are dismissed.
And there he goes--moving on without so much as a goodbye.
The Doctor may be done with you, Commander. But you and me, we're just getting started.
Years of planning... and research... destroyed by your utter incompetence! Pack your gear, Commander, and get off my planet!
The launcher... Destroyed! You are finished! Pack your gear, Commander, and get off my planet!
Impressive... For a Bug, the Hydra is remarkably efficient. Now finish off the remaining Arachnids and secure the sector completely.
Do not lose the Hydra Bug
Do not lose the D.I.M. Dart Launcher
The detonation achieved all primary yield objectives. It was quite... illuminating.
I need you to lead a recovery team into ground zero and collect soil samples. We must analyze the residual effects of the payload on the local environment.
We have a serious infestation problem in the sector, Commander. A local hive - and the Bugs have already begun nesting in the rubble.
Handle this 'infestation' however you see fit. Just bring me those samples.

Commander, use this opportunity to deploy our new toxic weapon bipeds. These vehicles utilize a concentrated corrosive aerosol specifically designed to dissolve the structural integrity of the Arachnid exoskeleton.
Commander, I have already instructed you to deploy the Alchemist bipeds--do not make me repeat myself again.
Heads up, Commander. Ghutana is crawling with Buzzers. These Bugs are built for chaos, capable of slipping through - or crashing through - even the tightest gaps in your defensive lines.
The crater is secure. Honestly, Commander, you're making this look easy. Excellent work.
The soil extractor is ready for deployment. We can save the congratulations for later. Place the extractor and finish the assignment.
Extractor is ready for activation on your mark. Just be ready for company--It's going to be a total Bug magnet once the drilling begins!
Here they come! Show 'em what the Federation is made of!
Deploy Bug Cages wherever you need to augment your defenses. I'll make sure you have plenty of specimens at your disposal.
Sample received. You've served your purpose for the day. Dismissed.
That local hive needs to be neutralized to secure the sector.
Head back to base, Commander--I'm looking forward to our debriefing. Don't keep me waiting.
Clear the crater of Buzzer Nests
Gather soil samples from the crater
Watch your step, Commander. This sector is basically a junk drawer for nuclear and bio-waste. It's not pretty, but it keeps the labs running.
Arachnid physiology is built for survival against the most extreme variables. We have detected fascinating mutations in direct response to our discarded materials.
Alas, the specimens are deceased - but this still provides a unique opportunity to study forced evolution.
Locate the cadavers and prepare them for extraction.
The XM3-A Raycaster biped is now available for field testing, Commander. Its concentrated microwave emitter provides an efficient way to neutralize Arachnids from a safe distance.
Use it to clear out the generic Spitter population… In nature, the elimination of the mediocre is the only way to reveal the exceptional.
XM3-A Raycasters are now ready for deployment.
Why are there still no Raycaster bipeds on the field?! My time is far too valuable to be spent echoing basic directives.
Commander, my scans found an old Federation outpost nearby. Bring it back online; I'm sure there's some hardware inside that'll make your life easier.
Specimen secured. Move to the next coordinate.
Fascinating... Proceed to the next carcass.
A productive acquisition... Continue the sweep.
Excellent. All carcasses are secured and accounted for.
Heads up, Commander. We've got a massive Bug signature heading straight for your position. Get ready... and happy hunting!
That’s the last of ‘em! Area's green and the sector is officially secure. Quite the performance, Commander!
Commander, we have an emergency at this weapon testing facility. Someone ignored safety protocols, and now the live 'target' specimens have broken out of their holding pens and overrun the place.
Doctor Kraus is on his way for a primary research test, and I'd really rather not deal with one of his tantrums today. Let's get to work and tidy up before he gets here.
Your drop zone is right outside the facility walls. Secure the main supply bay first, then proceed with the rest of the facility.
You're coming up on the supply bay. Secure the station before you sweep the rest of the facility.
Main supply base secured. You'll be able to call in reinforcements from here. Now you have to bring the rest of the facility back under our control.
Commander, you are authorized to clear all Arachnids in the facility's perimeter. That includes any Bugs still located in their holding pens.
The holding pens are cleared. If Kraus wants any more 'live test subjects' for his research, he's going to have to replenish his stock later.
Commander, Doctor Kraus has arrived in orbit over the facility...

It seems the security detachment has proven utterly incompetent. I hope you will do better, Commander. For your own sake. Take back the central control hub immediately, and I will grant access to the adjacent missile silos.
Control Center secured. You now have access to the missile silos.
To direct these missiles, you'll first need to deploy a Missile Specialist.
Missile Specialists are now available for deployment.
A Missile Specialist has just been dropped into the facility.
You will need to deploy a new Missile Silo before we can proceed.
Let's see what these missiles can do. Choose a target, send in a Missile Specialist and enjoy the spectacle.
I'm not surprised to see the extensive use of our missile silos. After all, the hypothesis that even a crude means of mindless destruction has its usefulness is why you are here.
Commander, the device up ahead is the focus of today's test program, and a vital part of the 'Hercules Program' - one of my most promising Arachnid research programs.

In terms you may understand: it can launch special darts with great precision. Darts designed to target the nerve stem of a very specific Arachnid specimen - and allow us to essentially take full control of its mind.
Needless to say, I want the D.I.M. Dart Launcher secured without a scratch.
Behold, the ultimate target of the Hercules Program: The Hydra - or at least a mockup of this magnificent Arachnid specimen.
Clear the area so my team can be deployed to observe the D.I.M. Dart firing test.
All systems are on line and everyone is in position. Commencing the D.I.M. dart test launch. Three... Two... One... Launch!

Excellent. The dart has survived the impact and has penetrated well within the required target area and depth to establish a neural connection. An important step toward the climax of the Hercules Program!
We've lost the main supply bay! Mission failed, Commander.
Clear the Hive near the Hydra Mockup
Do not lose the main base
Collect irradiated DNA samples from the nuclear facility
Another day, another toxic excursion. Doctor Kraus insists it is 'vital for his Hercules Program', of course.
You are stepping into an old abandoned nuclear facility. By the looks of it, the plant suffered a pretty violent termination.
The Doctor wants pheromone samples extracted from several irradiated Bug corpses. At least the fallout saved you the trouble of killing them first...
Just keep a close eye on your Geiger counter. And if it glows, keep your distance. I'm quite fond of your current number of limbs.
The radiation around that carcass is off the charts, Commander. Assign Hazmat Troopers to handle the extraction. Their suits provide the necessary shielding against levels this high.
Hazmat Troopers are now available for deployment. They can operate in high radiation zones without melting into a puddle.

Commander, I ran a search for 'glowing crawling abomination'. Nothing in the Federal database matches that mess... Keep your distance. Radiation signatures are extreme and they look like they're about to pop.

Commander, my scanners are showing large numbers of Hopper nests in the peaks surrounding the plant. I strongly suggest you restore the air defense system in the center of the facility before these Hoppers decide to come down for a closer look.
Heads up, Commander! We've got a whole swarm of Hoppers coming in fast from the mountains!
That's most of the Hoppers accounted for. But do keep one eye on the clouds.
That's another sample in the bag. One more carcass left to dissect.
Commander, the DNA samples have just arrived in my lab. We have all we need to proceed with the Hercules Program.
Great! Meet me at the medical bay, Commander. I'll check if you're growing anything that wasn't there before.
Collect DNA samples from Tanker carcasses
Deploy a squad of Hazmat Troopers
Test the Pheromone Emitter by defending it against escalating Bug waves

Commander, we're moving forward with the Hercules Program. Doctor Kraus is field testing his 'Pheromone Emitter' today. As far as I understand, this device will be used to lure in this elusive Hydra he keeps talking about.
Today we are just doing test runs, however. The first low-yield test already pulled in enough Bugs to overwhelm the facility's outer defenses.
Kraus calls it a success, but you'll need to clear out these infestations before the tests can proceed.
Good progress on clearing the infestation. Continue the sweep.
Inner perimeter cleared! The infestation has been purged.
Commander, we've found another infestation to the west of the facility. Clear it out.
These delays are unacceptable. I am initiating the second test phase now. I expect you to do your job and protect my Emitter.
Three... two... one. Emitter operating at forty percent capacity.
Bugs incoming! Hold the perimeter, Commander. Don't let them reach the Emitter.
I have arranged access to the central radio station. You can now use it to deploy reinforcements directly on top of the compound roof.
We are commencing the third test run. Emitter set to seventy percent capacity.
Another wave of Bugs incoming! You know what to do, Commander.
This is getting a little too close for comfort. Let's beef up our firepower with a few E-Pulse Cannons before the next wave pours in.
E-Pulse Cannons are in position and online. The perimeter is ready for the final round.
Initiating the final test run at full capacity. Stand by!
Looks like that's the whole sector bearing down on your position. Give them everything you've got!
The Emitter performed perfectly up to its maximum load. The data shows we are officially ready to proceed with the next phase of the Hercules Program. Excellent work, everyone.
Kraus seems happy. And you know I always am when I've seen you in action. Well done, Commander!
The Emitter is damaged beyond repair... You incompetent fool. You had one simple job and you messed it all up!
Do not lose the Pheromone Emitter
Deploy E-Pulse Cannons on the marked locations
Commander, our standard squads won't cut it for this next phase. Authorize deployment of the Fortis Eradicators—they're built to hold the line under heavy fire.
Fortis Eradicators are cleared for deployment. Get a squad on the ground before we fire up the Emitter again.
Restore order at Ghutana High Security Prison
While Kraus is busy planning the next phase of the Hercules Program, we've got a real fire to put out, Commander. A major riot broke out in Ghutana's infamous High Security Prison.
Damage to the facility is severe and with the security systems down, the local Arachnids have also crashed the party.
Between the armed inmates and Bugs looking for a snack, the situation is a total mess. You'll need to handle both to restore control.
You have the inner perimeter locked down tight. Just the way I like it, Commander.
We've picked up pockets of escapees in the wastes. They probably learned why escape on Ghutana is futile--the local swarm is much less forgiving than a cell block.
They're armed, but they have nowhere to run. Bring them to justice--by any means necessary.
First group neutralized. They should've stayed in their cells.
Another pocket of escapees has been dealt with. Good progress, Commander.
That should be the last of them. Any stragglers we missed will face the Bugs' justice system.
Commander, I've been monitoring the situation and found a practical use for the occasion.
I have successfully miniaturized the D.I.M. technology. It will still outright kill smaller Arachnids, but it should function on larger specimens like Tankers or Scorpions.
Deploy the projectile on a specimen of your choice, then use it to... 'neutralize' the remaining rioters in the courtyard.
Use the Overseer's D.I.M. dart launcher against a large specimen. Once the link is established, the creature is yours to command.
Neural link established. Now guide the subject to the prison courtyard and... let it loose on the rioters. I will monitor the procedure.
A successful trial. Scientific progression requires sacrifice, and today, these criminals provided the data I needed. Excellent work, Commander.
Everything's secure. The surviving prisoners are back under lock and key. Now come back to base and you can lock me down for debriefing.
Use the Mind Control Dart on a Tanker or Scorpion
Use the Mind Controlled Bug to clear the prisoners in the courtyard
Retrieve Emitter modules and clear the sector
Commander, Doctor Kraus has narrowed down the Hydra's hiding spot. To lure it in, he has ordered the deployment of the Pheromone Emitter in this sector.
We had dropships en route with the machine's modules, but an unusually high number of Acid Grenadiers turned the sky into a kill-zone.
Several ships went down, scattering the cargo across Bug territory...
Doctor Kraus is still unaware of this... hiccup, and I'd prefer to keep it that way. Get to the crash sites and retrieve all Emitter modules. I'm counting on you, Commander!
First module secure. Keep it up.
Another module in the bag. One more to go.

Commander, reports on those Acid Grenadiers are correct. Large numbers have been detected around the local hives. If we're going to resume transportation of the emitter modules, you'll have to deal with this threat.
That's one hive cleared. Good work!
Another hive cleared - just one more to go.
That was the last of them. All hives are cleared!
Heads up, Commander! Sensors show the Bugs found a new route into the sector. Keep our territory secured!
New incursion point detected, Commander. Bugs keep pouring in. Make sure there is no hole in your defenses.
Commander, Kraus has been itching for a field test on his new 'pheromone disruptor' grenades. Let's get him some valuable data to keep him distracted.

Don't ask me for the technical manual, but apparently, this substance rewrites a Bug's 'friend or foe' list. One whiff and they'll tear into anything that hasn't been sprayed. Toss a few of these grenades into the swarm and let's see some of that 'bug-on-bug' action Kraus is so excited about.
That's plenty of data on the pheromone disruptor. More than enough to keep the Doctor out of our hair for a while longer.
Clean sweep. Modules are on route and Kraus won't find out about the delay. I don't mind sharing a secret with you, Commander.
Retrieve Emitter modules from crashed dropships
Restore power and charge the Pheromone Emitter
Commander, you're on final approach to the Emitter construction site. I have Doctor Kraus on the line for your briefing.
Ah, Commander. This abandoned plant is the perfect foundation for our work. The new Pheromone Emitter is being assembled at the facility's core as we speak.
To run at full capacity it will need a massive power draw. Secure the perimeter and get those old turbines operational.
And Commander... I expect no delays this time.
Commander. We already have some defenses in place around the Emitter, but make sure the machine stays in one piece. If the Bugs tear it down, our mission--and the Doctor's temper--goes with it.

Commander... The Mass Emitter is gone, and Kraus is making enough noise to wake every Bug on the planet. I can't talk our way out of this one. Not the climactic finish I was hoping for, but your tour on Ghutana is terminated.
Power restored. Move to the next turbine.
All power turbines are up and running.
It's insufficient! The degradation of these turbines is more severe than anticipated.
We'll have to charge the high-capacity battery array just beyond the facility's perimeter. Deploy an XM11-K Annihilator and connect its nuclear reactor to this battery.
The Annihilator is on the ground, Doctor. What's the play?
The XM11-K is built on the robust Marauder chassis; its reactor has more than enough surplus to charge other devices. Move the unit into position near the battery to begin the transfer.
We're deep in the red zone, and the Bugs are sensitive to electrical surges. Expect company the moment the charging begins.
Battery link established... And we have massive Arachnid movement heading your way. Hang in there, Commander!
Battery is at 100% capacity. Are we good to go, Doctor?
Power output finally meets the required parameters. We are ready. Activating the Emitter... now.
Magnificent! I'm seeing a massive surge of bio-signatures on all sensors. Prepare yourself, Commander; you are about to witness the majesty of the Hydra.

No sign of the Hydra yet... but a remarkable large number of Acid Grenadiers once again. Physical similarities between the two species exist, but perhaps there is a stronger biological link than we expected?
The waves have ceased, yet the Hydra remains absent... I'll be in my lab... re-evaluating the data to determine why the Emitter failed to do its job. Do not disturb me.
You did a great job, Commander. While Kraus is busy with his R&D, you and I can meet for R&R.
Do not lose the Pheromone Emitter
Clear the Bug infestation in the Mining Tunnel
Welcome back, Commander. The situation here is... well, it's a bloodbath.
The local miners got careless, dug their tunnels into a Hive, and now the whole town got turned into Bug territory.
I need you to hold this outpost, clear that Hive, smash every Bug you encounter and remind the Arachnids that every inch of this rock is human territory!
You're almost at the tunnel. Alas, no survivors in the town... It's a total loss.
Heads up, Commander! Massive signatures are bearing down on the outpost.
I've already got dropships moving your squads back to the perimeter.
Get down there and defend the position like you mean it, Commander. I'll be watching the show!
I'd trust you to hold my borders any day of the week, Commander. See you back at base!

A sandstorm just swatted a dropship right out of the sky - deep in Bug territory. Word is, one of our top Generals was on board, and HQ wants to know if he's still breathing.
It's a mess out there, but I know you can handle a little heat. Go find our VIP.
Dropship's clear, but bad news for the General. The survivors say he was incapacitated during a Bug attack and got dragged off toward the nearby Hive.
We cannot allow the Arachnids to 'pick his brain'--literally. Find him, and get him out - or make sure there's nothing left for the Bugs to extract.
Fresh blood on the sand, Commander. It's human. The target is in that Hive--get moving.
VIP is off the ground. Nice work, Commander!
Massive signatures are closing in on your position...
Hold the line--we want you back home in one piece!
You never cease to impress, Commander. Once you've got the blood and sand out of your cracks, meet me for debrief.

Rescue the General from the Hive

You'll need a radio operator to extract the civilians.
Defeat the Tanker in the Hydro Plant
We've got a crisis at the hydro-plant, Commander. Comm-chatter mentioned a Tanker breaching the defenses from below, breaking the perimeter from the inside, but I can't confirm that yet.
Regardless, Bugs keep pouring into the facility. Set up your defenses and halt the incursion.
You'll need more Materiel for those Turrets, Commander. Deploy a Materiel Depot to increase your stockpiles.
The defense is holding. Still zero evidence of a Tanker breach on my scans, though. Sweep the plant and get that control station back online.
I've got a distress signal from some civilians huddled up in that settlement. Get a Radio Operator on-site to coordinate a dropship evacuation.
You'll need a radio operator to extract the civilians.
I stand corrected! The Tanker is very real and it's right on top of you. Put it back in the dirt, Commander!
Standard rounds aren't going to cut it. Equip your troopers with grenades if you want to crack that Tanker's armor!
Efficient - and not afraid to get your hands dirty! Head back to base, Commander - you've earned yourself a hot shower.

Reports are confirming that more Bug hives have been eradicated in this sector.
Another source of Arachnid terror has been purged. Peace and safety is returning to the galaxy.

I'm afraid the mission isn't over yet, though.

Well done commander, that went pretty smooth.

This Battle Group is focused on experimental chemical and radiation weapons, as well as the application of pheromonal and neurochemical technology to manipulate and control the behavior of Arachnid specimens.
Doctor Kraus spearheads the most advanced weapons research on Ghutana. His primary focus: the hunt for the elusive Hydra.
New chemical, radiation and biological weapons unleashed!
Would you like to know more about The Eradicators DLC?
These specialists direct a pack of drugged Bugs against enemy units. They are equipped with air pressure guns that fire poison darts.
These troopers are equipped with acid-based grenade launchers that are effective against medium armored targets, while their suits offer protection against chemical and radiation hazards.

The 'Fortis' powered armor suit provides increased battlefield survivability while the E-Pulse 92 weapon fires energy projectiles up to a medium firing range, which are effective against medium armored targets and deal area-of-effect damage on impact.
These troopers are equipped with prototype weapons that can fire deadly radiation beams through multiple enemies, while their advanced powered armor suits offer excellent protection and mobility.
This lightly armored biped is equipped to unleash a cocktail of deadly acid-based weapons. Its robotic arm also allows it to construct various defensive structures and weapons.
This biped can fire a highly concentrated radiation beam with great precision, making it very effective at engaging lightly armored targets over a long distance. It can also call down reinforcements.
This squad is equipped with a multi-barreled Rocket Launcher to counter heavily armored threats. They also have the authorization to call in strikes from any missile silo in the sector.
This heavy biped specializes in pheromone weapon technology. It can turn the larger Arachnids types against their own hive, or even take direct control over an individual specimen.

This experimental configuration of the M11 biped is armed with a powerful radiation weapon and dual missile launchers. In addition, its nuclear reactor can boost the performance of nearby Irradiator squads.
A subterranean missile silo that provides various types of powerful long range missiles to the Missile Specialists.
A small Arachnid variant bred for speed and chaos. When an enemy is nearby, the creature uses its wings to dash across the terrain with great speed.

These projectiles generally transmute into corrosive acid on impact, but curiously, some globs have been found to contain live Buzzer Bugs. A sickly and heavily mutated Arachnid type which detonates when it attacks an enemy, or when it is killed. This explosion deals short range blast damage, as well as radiation damage over a wider radius.
A massive and heavily armored Arachnid specimen. Handle with extreme caution.

Release artificial pheromones that effectively conceal the presence of the troopers from nearby Arachnids

Deploy a 'Remotely Piloted Vehicle' that can be directed to unleash deadly radiation damage on enemies below.
Fires a missile filled with poison gas at a target location, dealing area-of-effect damage to all units in the area-of-effect radius.
Employ the Annihilator's dual rocket tubes as a make-shift jetpack to jump toward more advantageous positions.

Ah, our Horde Handlers. Do not let their Arachnid escort unsettle you. Through pheromonal recalibration, we have co-opted their predatory instincts to serve our interests.
Unlike your troopers, they are free from any psychological limitations - they simply exist to kill. A remarkable display of biological utility.

However, we still require access to the hangar for refueling operations. It appears the Arachnids have already established a nest within the structure-- a fascinating reappropriation of our infrastructure.
Incoming signatures are spiking. It's fascinating... the Arachnids seem to possess an instinctual awareness of the threat we've prepared for them.
I'm sorry, Commander... Doctor Kraus has already requested a replacement for your position. It looks like your tour on Ghutana is terminated.

Commander, we know why the Mass Pheromone Emitter ultimately failed to draw in the Hydra. Tracing the trail of Acid Grenadiers back to its source led us to a massive lair... filled with millions of eggs.
Right at the center of it all: our Hydra. The creature possesses hive-minded instincts that drive it to guard this nest. Instincts far outweighing the lure of our pheromone technology!
Now we must proceed with care. This is a priceless opportunity to study the Arachnids' behavioral systems.
Commander, secure a cluster of eggs and send them to my lab. And restrain yourself - I need them intact.
Do not provoke the Hydra yet. I'm aware this procedure requires a level of nuance and intellect your military branch is not known for. Complete your tasks and follow my instructions to the letter.
As for the surrounding hordes, exterminate them all. They are of minimal scientific value.
Commander! Protect the Hydra with everything you have! The lives of you and your troopers are inconsequential next to the potential loss of this specimen!
Wait... I'll direct it... I'll turn it against the incoming hordes! Form a perimeter around the Hydra, and I'll demonstrate what this majestic beast is capable of!
I'm transferring the Hydra to the Research Division's high-security transport immediately.
Years of planning... and research... destroyed by the magnitude of your incompetence! Report back to base, Commander. I assure you a court martial will be the least of your worries.
The launcher... Destroyed! The mission... a shambles. You are finished! Pack your gear, Commander, and get off my planet!
A masterpiece of biological engineering. Finish off the remaining Arachnids and secure the sector completely.
Commander... Kraus is having a complete meltdown over the loss of that extractor. It looks like your tour on Ghutana is already terminated...
Handle this 'infestation' however you see fit. Just retrieve those samples for me.

Commander, use this opportunity to deploy our new XM3-C Alchemist bipeds. These vehicles utilize a concentrated corrosive aerosol specifically designed to dissolve the structural integrity of the Arachnid exoskeleton.
XM3-C Alchemists are now ready for deployment.
HQ wants you to clear out that hive before we call it a day.
Can't leave a job half-finished, right?
HQ is getting uneasy about that Hive, Commander... You should deal with it asap.
Good work. The Hive has been cleared.
Use it to clear out the generic Spitter population... In nature, the elimination of the mediocre is the most reliable method to reveal the exceptional.
Commander, there's a decommissioned base just a few clicks from your position. Take control of the facility and I'll authorize a requisition for the surplus gear inside.
An interesting find... Proceed to the next carcass.
Contact! Multiple signatures detected and they are closing in fast. Lock and load, Commander--show 'em what the Federation is made of!
That's the last of 'em! Area's green and the sector is officially secure.
That's the most impressive performance I've seen from you yet, Commander... on the field.
I'll see you back at base. Don't keep me waiting.
Can't wait to see you back home - for debriefing, of course.
I'm clearing my schedule for our debriefing. See you soon.
Commander, you are authorized to put down any Arachnids within the facility's perimeter. That includes any Bugs still located in their holding pens.
It seems the security detachment has proven utterly incompetent. I hope you will do better, Commander. For your own sake.
Take back the central control hub immediately, and I will grant access to the adjacent missile silos.
To direct these missiles, you'll first need to deploy a squad of Missile Specialists.
A squad of Missile Specialists has just been dropped into the facility.
Commander, remember to deploy Missile Specialists if you want to make use of the Missile Silos.
Let's see what these missiles can do. Choose a target, send in your Missile Specialists and enjoy the spectacle.
I'm not surprised to see such extensive use of our missile silos. After all, the hypothesis that even a crude mind is capable of ample destruction is why you are here.

To put it simply in terms you may understand: it can launch special darts with great precision. Darts designed to target the nerve stem of a very specific Arachnid specimen - and allow us to essentially take full control of its mind.
All systems are online and everyone is in position. Commencing the D.I.M. dart test launch.

Excellent. The dart has survived the impact and has penetrated well within the required target area and depth to establish a neural connection. You should feel privileged to have participated in such an important step toward the culmination of the Hercules Program!
Just keep a close eye on your surroundings. If it glows, keep your distance. I'm quite fond of your current number of limbs.
The radiation around that carcass is off the charts, Commander. Assign Hazmat Troopers to handle the specimen extraction. Their suits provide the necessary shielding against levels this high.
Commander, remember to deploy Hazmat Troopers. They are equipped to withstand toxic and radiation hazards.

Commander, I ran a search for 'glowing crawling abomination'. Nothing in the Federal database matches that mess... Radiation signatures are extreme and they look like they're about to pop. Deploying Hazmat Troopers against them is your best bet.
Commander, my scanners are showing large numbers of Hopper nests in the peaks surrounding the plant.
I strongly suggest you restore the air defense system in the center of the facility before these Hoppers decide to come down for a closer look.
Kraus calls it a success, but you'll need to clear out these infestations before more tests can proceed.
Excellent, the western flank of the compound has been secured.
Initiating the second test run. Three... two... one...
Emitter operating at forty percent capacity.
Commander, remember to deploy E-Pulse Cannons at the marked locations. We really need the extra firepower.
Kraus seems happy. And you know I always enjoy you working up a sweat. Well done, Commander!
E-Pulse troopers have been deployed. Instruct them to set up E-Pulse Cannons at the marked locations.
We've picked up pockets of jailbreakers in the wastes. They probably learned why escape on Ghutana is futile--the local hordes are much less forgiving than a cell block.
That should be the last of them. Any stragglers we missed will face the Bugs' penal system.
I have successfully miniaturized the D.I.M. technology. It will still outright kill smaller Arachnids, but it should function as designed on larger specimens like Tankers or Scorpions.
Deploy an XM9-B Overseer and launch the projectile on a specimen of your choice, then use it to... 'neutralize' the remaining rioters in the courtyard.
Commander, I have instructed the deployment of an Overseer biped--do not make me repeat myself again.
Neural link established. Now guide the subject to the prison courtyard and... discharge it upon the rioters. I will monitor the results.
Everything's secure. The surviving prisoners are back under lock and key. Hmmm, that gives me an idea for our debriefing. Hurry back to base.
Commander, Doctor Kraus has narrowed down locations for the Hydra's hiding spot. To lure it out, he has ordered the deployment of the Mass Pheromone Emitter in this sector.

Commander, activity reports on those Acid Grenadiers are accurate. Large numbers have been detected around the local hives. If we're going to resume transportation of the emitter modules, you'll have to deal with this threat.
Approach those Acid Grenadiers with caution, Commander. Their armor is thick, and the clusters of volatile bile they launch can melt through hull plating and infantry alike.
A new breach has opened up. Don't let any Bugs slip through the cracks, Commander.
Don't ask me for the technical manual, but apparently, this substance rewrites a Bug's 'friend or foe' neural pathways. One whiff and they'll tear into anything that hasn't been sprayed.
Toss a few of these grenades into the horde and let's see some of that Bug-on-Bug action Kraus is so hot and bothered about.
Commander, remember to deploy Irradiator squads and put their pheromone disruptor grenades to the test. If not for Doctor Kraus, then do it for me.
Clean sweep. Modules are en route and Kraus shouldn't find out about the delay. Of course, I don't mind sharing a secret with you, Commander.
Commander, you're on final approach to the Mass Emitter construction site. I have Doctor Kraus on the line for your briefing.

Ah, Commander. This abandoned plant is the perfect foundation for our work. Two D.I.M. Dart Launchers are already in place, and the new Pheromone Emitter is being assembled at the facility's core as we speak.
Commander. We already have some defenses in place around the Emitter, but make sure the machine stays in one piece. If the Bugs tear it down, our mission--and the Doctor's patience--goes with it.
Commander, remember to deploy an Annihilator and move it to the Battery Array.
No sign of the Hydra yet... but a remarkably large number of Acid Grenadiers have appeared once again.
Physical similarities between the two species exist, but perhaps there is a stronger biological link than we expected?
Don't let the doctor get to you, Commander. You did great work down there. And while Kraus is busy with his R&D, you and I can meet for some R&R.

original: The weapons lab established on planet Ghutana has been developing new ways to kill bugs using various chemical substances.
But carelessness toward the Arachnid test subjects has led to disaster. Someone failed to follow proper safety protocols, and vengeful Bugs have quickly taken over the place.

An M.I. detachment has just descended into the facility. While the mishap is unfortunate, the situation does provide an excellent opportunity to field test some of these new chemical weapons. When life gives you pests, make pesticide.
Some of the test subjects are still locked safely within enclosed basins. But to deal with the security breach, protocol demands all Arachnid life forms within the facility must be destroyed.
It appears the Arachnids have caused considerable damage to the facility and have dug their way into local tunnel systems.
The M.I. will have to smoke them out of these caves.
There is a hall of large centrifuges just around the corner, used for the refinement of deadly chemicals. Security footage also reveals a strong Arachnid presence crawling around these machines.
Just as the all-clear was given for the interior of the chemical weapons lab, reports have come in of an Arachnid horde heading for the facility's main gate.

The Arachnid threat inside and around the lab has finally been eliminated. It may take time to replenish the required test subjects and scientists, but these new chemical weapons have certainly proven their effectiveness.
It looks like the facility was cleared just in time. The thin line of troopers holding the outside gate will need all the help they can get.
The facility can be accessed through several top-side landing platforms. These are intended for the shipping of supplies and personnel but may now prove useful to deploy reinforcements.
The M.I. has failed to secure the chemical lab using the very weapons that were being developed there. The best answer to the Bug threat clearly remains hot lead and explosive firepower.
Chemical Troopers are immune to poison gas

original: How the hell did bugs get through the perimeter line? Those defences were iron tight!
Perhaps, but this air base certainly wasn’t designed to repel an attack.
Why establish an airbase here anyway?  These aircraft could be safe in orbit – now they’re just asking to be attacked.
I’m sure Command had their reasons.
Power troopers are dropping to secure an initial landing spot.
It's going to be a long night.
There are Bug Lairs around the tower. Take them all out.
Hangars secured! Get those strikes rolling!
That area has been declared secure.
The tower area has been secured. Main force ready to drop.
Next we'll have to clear the rest of the airfield, including the Power Plant, ...
Once that's done, we hold onto it no matter what the Bugs throw at us.
It looks like they have finally had enough!
Excellent work, but there’s no time to rest. Get to the shuttles, I have another task for you.
On the Sky Marshal’s orders, of course.
They’re coming from every direction. Stay on your toes.
Maintain a 360-degree watch! You see an enemy, move to intercept!
Another attack is on its way!
Congratulations on a most convincing performance. The trap has been sprung!
This airfield was just bait. Command created a target the Bugs could not resist to lure them out of their holes. Let them through the front line to be exposed out in the open.
But what about the aircraft? If they were destroyed...
They were never going to fly in the first place.  We built empty shells, fakes.  The real ones are airborne right now.  For once, it’s the Bugs who have underestimated us.
Next time you pull a stunt like this, I would appreciate being kept in the loop. Anyway, at least the plan worked. If the Federation wanted a target rich environment, they’ve got it.
Well that did not go to plan.
As predicted, the bugs are expending maximum effort to retake the airfield.

original: Come in, anybody. Any one? It’s a massacre out there.
Plasma bugs were waiting for us, blew our shuttles out of the sky.
Rocket troopers are down! We're done for.
Use the rocket launchers and ammo crates from the dropship. You'll need their extra reach.
Comms are shot to hell, we can't get through to request pickup.
Our best chance is to fight our way west to a local relay station. From there we should be able to contact Fleet
Glad to hear your voice, colonel, I knew you’d pull through.
What’s your status? Command’s upset the advance is behind schedule.
There’s not going to be any advance! Do they have any idea what happened down here?
Intel is still sketchy. Only a few of the drop teams have radioed us so far.
Those might be the only ones left!
It's bad out there. We need pick up.
That's a no-go on pick up. Plasma bugs to the South of your position are making the approach too hot for shuttles. You take them out, we'll find some pilots crazy enough to come get you.
Roger that. Lets go take out those plasma bugs.
Looks like we've out stayed our welcome. Time to leave this party. Where are those shuttles?
Pick up is a no go. All hell's breaking loose in orbit, at least two ships have taken direct hits. You're going to have to try and make it out on foot.
This just gets better and better. Our only chance is to split into small groups, stay low and move fast. That way least some of us should see tomorrow.
Command has ordered a general retreat. Get your people ready for evacuation
A lot of them are not going to make it. We have their locations, but heavy plasma bug fire means Command can’t risk the shuttles to make pick up. Your people are the lucky ones...
Negative, we’re not leaving. The MI leaves no trooper behind. Send over the coordinates of those plasma bugs. We’ll take em out and clear a path for the shuttles.
That's a big call to make on your own, colonel. There's a hell of a lotta bugs guarding them. If this goes wrong, it's on your head.
Wouldn’t have it any other way.
We've reached some of the survivors.
We've got a distress call coming in from another group of survivors. If you can get to them, we could sure use their help.
Come on you apes, join a squad and get back into action!
Intel estimates must have been wrong. The Bugs are already here.
That horde of bugs is here. Destroy the last Plasmas and get out!
You're going to have to pick up the pace. We've got bug readings off the dial closing on your location
Great, as if we needed the extra motivation.
Inform Command that we're looking at a total loss.
Godammnit! How many more people are we going to lose today?

original: Is this all?  Is this everyone that’s made it?  Damn it, we lost a lot of good people.
This canyon’s the only way home. I don’t like it, but there’s no other choice.
After last night’s fiasco, this whole area is enemy territory.
The map shows some old bases up ahead. Abandoned a while ago, but they’re our best chance.
...so stay sharp and keep a lookout for other survivors. We can’t be the only ones that got out.
Hang in there, we're almost at the radio station. Might be a bit dusty, but they should have a functioning transmitter.
Once we’re there we can take a breather and wait for pickup
Damnit, guess we’re not using that radio.
There should be another transmitter further on.
That was neatly done. But we've got to keep moving forward.
Can you hear that? Bugs are coming.
Set up an ambush on the high ground. Hold fire until the bugs are square in the killzone!
We’re picking up your signal. Do you read me?
Loud and clear. Am I glad to hear your voice, major! Requesting immediate evac.
Negative, request denied. Based on your position, Command has new instructions. A large force of bugs is approaching. You have orders to hold your position and slow their advance.
We won’t even be a speed bump for those bugs! That isn’t a fight we can win.
You don’t have to win, just keep the bugs busy for a bit.
Ava, I am not throwing these troopers’ lives away for nothing...
You need to follow orders. The Federation will remember your bravery.
Sorry, you’re breaking up. Repeat that please.
Damn interference. Couldn’t hear what she was saying. Guess we should get outta here before the bugs arrive.
Listen, this is my call.  Command left us to die, but I am going to get you out of this.  Now let’s go kick some bug ass.
We made it - No thanks to those a-holes at HQ.
Hey, do you read us? These confounded radios have been on the fritz all day.
I’m sending pickup, but don’t think your little stunt went unnoticed. There will be consequences for this...
Inform Command that we're looking at a total loss
We don't have the firepower to take that Hive out.  Just get past it and keep going.
Transmitters online. Cross your fingers, let’s hope someone hears this.
Keep your asses moving, and watch out for bugs behind us!
Watch your feet, bugs under the sand!
Found more survivors. Troopers, follow us if you want to stay alive.
Looks like some of the others made it this far.  Fall in, troopers.

original: So, tell me about this deathtrap you’ve sent us into.  Any word from the advance squads?
We don’t know the situation underground. It’s safe to assume that bugs still control the mine tunnels.
Roger that. All right troopers, let’s go on a bug hunt! I want every inch of these mines cleared!
These doors are locked. Must have been trying to stop the bugs
You'll need to get to the control room to get them open.
Control Room is back online. Remotely accessing door locks...
Goddamnit. All friendly units down. Mission failed.
Tanker bug! Keep your distance from that thing!
Tanker's down! Regroup and move up.
Looks like it’s wounded. We can take this thing down with grenades.
Big chamber up ahead. Looks like the bugs enlarged it to make room for something.
Heads up. Security cameras reveal bugs on the way!
Bugs are down.  What you got for us next, Cortez?
Colonel, cameras are picking up a group of survivors trapped further down the mine.
Alright, let's go rescue these boys and girls.
Fine job on the rescue Colonel.  But we're detecting multiple bug contacts beyond that door.
Alright, roger that.  You new guys, lock and load.  We're gonna kill some bugs.
Congrats troopers, two tankers down in one day! When we get back topside, feel free to push those bragging rights.
There’s one of the advance teams. Troopers, you’re coming with us.
More of our guys! Glad we ran into them.
We have to take out that nest before continuing.
I hear movement, and it ain’t coming on two legs. Defensive formation! Maintain a clear field of fire.
That’s it for now. Move up.
Damnid, the corridor is blocked. No other choice but to go through this tunnel and see if we can find another route.
Finally out of Archie's caves... This should position us on the far end of the Control Room.
We’re on bug home turf, so be ready for the worst.

Here they come again. Keep shooting, rinse and repeat.
Reinforcements just left the ships. They’ll be entering the atmosphere momentarily.
Hold on people, we’re almost through this. Tomorrow’s a new day to die.
This bridgehead is the last line of defense. If it goes, there’s nothing between bugs and the refugee camps.
Please keep those civilians safe. We need them back in the factories when all this is over.
Reinforcements will come across when they can, but Command is keeping a tight rein on their supplies.
It’s all up to you. Don’t let those Arachnids get past.
Hell yes, here comes the cavalry! Counter-attacking troopers are dropping in behind enemy lines.
We need to get one of those stations up and running...
...then we can start taking this city back.
More reinforcements have arrived in the city.
Well, that's the surface clear. But those tunnels are still full of Bugs. I pity whoever's going to have to go down there and clear them out...
The bug hive in the middle of the city is exceptionally powerful. I would advise not engaging it until you have secured the rest of the area.
I'm not not one for backing down from a fight.
An admirable quality in a warfighter, but trust me on this one.  Wait until the other hives have been taken out - then you'll get your chance.
Base is online! Call down some backup.
Okay, let’s drive those bugs back to the river.

We've taken the traffic control center. Cameras are coming online and we have access to all the city's traffic gates.  Makes it easier for us to get around and also means we can funnel the Bugs' movements.
The city’s traffic control room is nearby. If we can reach it, we’ll gain remote access over the cameras and security gates. Might come in handy.
Hm... yes, that could be advantageous.
Seems like military intelligence doesn’t know everything.
Sensors are picking up strong Bug activity in the metro tunnels beneath the city.  I'd suggest you organize your troops into defensive positions.
Another strong reading from the underground sensors.
Looks like the Bugs are pretty pissed we stomped one of their nests.  Get yourselves ready people!
Another attack wave is heading for the foothold!

original: Take position on the left flank to get clear lines of fire!
We’ve thinned em out. Let’s move forward.
Advance team located the bug hole. Hope they saved something for us to shoot.
We can’t shoot through our own troops. Not without filing a lot of paperwork after.
The advance team kicked an anthill, now they got more bugs than they know what to do with. We’re here to save their asses.
Let’s do this by the book - don’t be a hero, and you won’t need a body bag.
Do you understand me? Let’s go, on the bounce!
TAC fighter strike incoming. Stand back and enjoy the fireworks.
They don’t like to get their uniforms dirty, but those fly boys are pretty useful sometimes.
Damn, a few bugs got away. Get after them, before they reach the settlement!
What kind of half-assed containment operation is this?
Sir, Major Cortez reporting. Orders from Command require you to confiscate all civilian weapons.
That’s a copy. Good to hear your voice.
Squad, secure those weapon stashes - not that these guys will be using them.
Let that be a lesson. These colonists had guns, but they didn’t have training or discipline. That’s why we’re alive and they’re not.
There’s a radio tower ahead of your position. It should be able to cut through the interference and get you some reinforcements.
Radio station’s just ahead. Move into range and get Fleet on the horn. Finally, we can break through this goddamn interference
Our mission is to get some reinforcements!
These apes have taken a lickin’. Use the radio station to call up Fleet and get replacements for our casualties.
Sir, Command just radioed out an alert. Major bug movement to your east.
OK. Things are about to get interesting. Look sharp, people. Form a perimeter.
Here they come. Watch your fields of fire.
We've failed.  Can't complete the mission now.
Welcome to Delta IV.  Now haul ass and get behind those walls.
Outstanding! This area’s hotter than we thought.
New orders, sir. Bug activity is too strong. Command is recalling you to Delta IV base. Leave the Civvies and get yourself home.
That route won’t be pretty. Rough terrain, lots of hidey holes for bugs. But you gotta punch through.
Battle’s over. Open up, you rookies.
We’re not done yet. Get on those walls and get ready.
Alright you apes. Show those bugs what you’re made of.
Well done, troopers. Any wounded head to the medic. Everyone else, go find yourself a drink.
Bugs are going for the base. Standard procedure is to keep the gate shut until there are zero hostiles in the area.
Ah hell, guess you’re doing this in the open. At least it’ll be a target-rich environment.
Shit, this operation is a complete Charlie Foxtrot. Mission failed.
Sounds like the other company’s in trouble. Let’s lend ’em a hand.
Damn it. Either these civilians ignored the evac order or someone’s getting a whipping back at base for missing these stragglers.
Chariot bugs, small, but there’s no such thing as a harmless bug. Splat ‘em and keep moving.
Allied units block line of fire
Move Here for clear Line of Fire
Use Engineers to burn through the hedges
Follow the road into the town

Fleet’s about to drop the hammer, so those bugs are desperate to escape.
It's not ideal.  Some of these fortifications are FUBAR . . . but we'll work with what we've got.
We will hold them here while the TAC Fighters unleash hell on Earth.
You mean hell on Kwalasha. Not that this planet was any Eden to begin with.
Must I remind you to tighten your defenses?! We can't afford to let too many bugs escape.
Bugs keep slipping past. You need to get a grip on the situation before it's too late.
Too many Bugs have escaped. The plan is failing!
Fighter pilots have reported bugs slipping through the perimeter.
They have intercepted the threat, but tracking individual targets is not the Fleet's responsibility.
Make sure this does not happen again. If the bugs break through, the whole ruse was for nothing.
The Sky Marshal came up with this plan?
I may have assisted the slightest bit.
The plan worked better than we could have hoped. But that does mean there are more bugs out there than had been anticipated.
Command is increasing the resources available for your battle group
The cave is sealed. The bugs won't be slipping through there any more.
Bugs have infiltrated through the mountains.
Clear that cave right now. I want that route sealed off.
Supply base has been brought online.  Just in time, we need more boots on the ground.
Another supply base is up and running. Use it.
That means things are about to get hairy. Every bug is going to swarm this way.
Another swarm of bugs is coming in.
The bugs are making another attempt at a breakthrough
Heads up, more bugs incoming. You know the drill by now.

Do not lose the main base

original: We got bugs on all sides. Nowhere to run.
Retreat is not an option. Keep fighting til you’re dead!
A brave sentiment, but your deaths won’t be necessary... today.
Reinforcements should arrive any minute. Until then, I suggest holding that compound.
Every weapon in the Federation’s arsenal has its place. But I’ll grant these M11 Babars are more useful on planets we want to keep.
Take good care of those Marauders. They’re on loan from General Rico.
Aw, we have to give them back?
The reinforcements have arrived to get you out of the city
Marauder team, clean up the bugs, take out the bug lairs.
Let’s see what you can do!
Push forward into the city center.
No slacking off! Just because the Marauders are here, doesn’t mean everyone else can take it easy.
Those things are powerful, but they're not invulnerable. We've got to look after the Marauders.
The defenders can't hold much longer.
Bugs are inside the compound! They're done for.
Package is down. We've failed to extract the officer!
The compound can't hold for much longer. I reckon we've got 5 minutes before the Bug's break in.
That compound won’t hold. Evacuate across the bridge, while you still can.
But the Sky Marshal said “Not one step back.”
We don’t always need to take those speeches literally...
The officer has reached safety. Let us hope the others' sacrifice was worth it.
The compound is going to fall.
We need that officer extracted to safety on the other side of the bridge.
Understood. We'll have to go around the compound to avoid running into Bug assaults. The only available route looks to be through the purification plant to the south-east.
Good work. Those Marauders are worth their weight in gold.
Bugs have infiltrated across the river. We're going to need to clear this bank if we're going to preserve the civilian workforce
Roger that. We'll take out those hives before they can spread.
Inform Command that we're looking at a total loss.
Package is down. We've failed to extract the officer!
More MI holding out! Let's get them out of trouble.
Ambush! They were waiting for us!
A smart strategy, for bugs. These warriors are being directly controlled by a ruling caste insect.
You mean a brain bug. There’s one on Kwalasha?
If there wasn’t, we would have won already.
The Arachnids have the city entrance blockaded.
Not for long. We’ll travel up the highway, kill anything that crawls.
There's a crap load of Bugs coming down the road!
Another Marauder has arrived. Give those bugs hell, captain.
Where have these been all my life?

Following years of brutal struggle, our forces on Kwalasha have finally isolated and trapped the Brain Bug orchestrating the Arachnid hordes on the planet.\n\nA vicious battle still lies ahead but we must seize this opportunity to cut off the head of the monster and bring an end to its reign of terror.
Help clearing the hive on the left flank
